short: `zaf hub`: the live view and its control page
is: The hub: what reads a project, or every project on the zaf home's list, into one state, draws it as a terminal frame or serves it as a page on the LAN, and admits the keyed controls that page may run.
conventions: Reading changes nothing and costs no model turns; only a `POST /api/<control>` the guard admitted changes state
The control key lives in the hub's memory only: never in a file, a log, the page's source or a Debug print
State is derived on every read (slots, live claims, Next for you); nothing is stored between frames
The server is the standard library's TcpListener with a thread a connection, so the hub adds no dependency

fs.name: controls.rs
fs.role: Controls: what the caller hands the server, the zaf home and what runs each control; a control with nothing behind it is an unknown route

fs.name: dashboard.rs
fs.role: the HTTP server: `GET /` the page, `/events` a frame per report, `/api/events` the change stream, `/api/state` the machine state as JSON; any other method 405, a POST without the key 403

fs.name: dashboard/
fs.role: assets.rs (the files of zaf/web/dist embedded at compile time, a fixed table) and tests

fs.name: draw.rs
fs.role: a Snapshot as a frame of text, pure

fs.name: gather.rs
fs.role: the board, ledger, slots, phases and last reports into a Snapshot; a task shows where the core places it (shown_state)

fs.name: guard.rs
fs.role: the Key made at start from the OS's random source and the Guard that checks the X-Zaf-Key header before a control gets any work; Guard::link is the key's one way out

fs.name: hook.rs
fs.role: what the profiles' PostToolUse hook reports: one general word for a tool call and who made it, the command never kept

fs.name: link.rs
fs.role: `zaf hub link`: a Unix socket in the zaf home (mode 0600) that hands the control link to the same user, refusing a caller with a live instance above it

fs.name: live.rs
fs.role: the process table: running launches, free slots, claims of ended instances, read again on every redraw

fs.name: lock.rs
fs.role: one serving hub a machine: the lock file in the zaf home naming the holder and its port, taken over when the holder is dead

fs.name: next.rs
fs.role: Next for you: what waits on the Engineer across all projects, most blocking first (unsigned epic, question or door, ready work no scheduler ticks, a phase that got nowhere, a project that cannot run)

fs.name: phases.rs
fs.role: the phases a model declares and reports with `zaf progress`, one file per task and role under .zaf/hub/plans

fs.name: reports.rs
fs.role: `.zaf/hub/reports`: one line per report, the last MAX_LINES kept; a write never fails its caller

fs.name: service.rs
fs.role: the systemd user unit that runs `zaf hub --port <n>`: install and remove behind a Systemctl trait

fs.name: state.rs
fs.role: ProjectState: one project's epics, queue and running instances as one JSON value; an unreachable board is a reason in plain words, not an error

fs.name: state/
fs.role: machine.rs (MachineState: every listed project read at once on its own thread under one deadline, headed by the machine line; a missing project kept and marked) and tests

fs.name: tests.rs
fs.role: the hub's unit tests; tests/liveness.rs is the fixture the liveness tests stand on

fs.name: watch.rs
fs.role: the terminal wait: redrawn when a report arrives, never on a timer

notes: Designed in docs/zaf-actions.md §5 and Forgejo epic #1 (the control hub)
The loops that feed the page and the processes that run a tick or a watch live in cli/hub/; this module never names an adapter
The page itself is zaf/web, served from its committed build
guard/, hook/, link/, lock/, next/, service/ and watch/ hold only tests.rs
